subject: english-language
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: How many marks in total are awarded for Section A (Directed Writing) on Paper 2?
questions.explain: Directed Writing carries 40 marks in total, made up of reading and writing marks.

questions.q: Within the 40 marks for Directed Writing, how many marks are awarded for reading?
questions.explain: Fifteen of the 40 Directed Writing marks assess how well candidates read and use the source material.

questions.q: How many of the Directed Writing marks are awarded for writing?
questions.explain: Twenty-five of the 40 Directed Writing marks assess the quality of the candidate's writing.

questions.q: What is the recommended length of a Directed Writing response?
options: 100-150 words
250-350 words
350-450 words
500-600 words
questions.explain: The Directed Writing task should be answered in roughly 250 to 350 words.

questions.q: Why should candidates use their own words rather than copy from the reading text in Directed Writing?
options: To demonstrate understanding of the ideas rather than simply lifting them
Because copying is always faster than paraphrasing
Because the reading text contains deliberate factual errors
To make the response much longer than required
questions.explain: Using own words shows the reading marks criterion of understanding and developing ideas, not lifting text.

questions.q: A Directed Writing task asks for a formal report to the head teacher. Which register is most appropriate?
options: Formal and objective, using standard English
Chatty and full of slang
Highly poetic with extended metaphors
Abbreviated, like a text message
questions.explain: A report for an authority figure requires a formal, objective register in standard English to suit purpose and audience.

questions.q: You must write a speech persuading fellow students to join a recycling scheme. Which technique is most suitable?
options: Rhetorical questions and direct address to engage the audience
Dense statistical tables with no commentary
A dictionary-style list of definitions
A private diary entry describing your feelings
questions.explain: A persuasive speech suits rhetorical questions and direct address, which fit the form, purpose and audience.

questions.q: What is the recommended length of a Section B composition?
options: 150-250 words
250-350 words
350-450 words
600-700 words
questions.explain: A Section B composition should be around 350 to 450 words.

questions.q: How are the 40 marks for a Section B composition divided?
options: 16 marks for content and structure, 24 marks for style and accuracy
24 marks for content and structure, 16 marks for style and accuracy
20 marks for content, 20 marks for accuracy
15 marks for reading, 25 marks for writing
questions.explain: Composition marks are split into 16 for content and structure and 24 for style and accuracy.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of descriptive writing?
options: To create a vivid impression of a place, person or scene through detail
To narrate a sequence of exciting events with a climax
To argue persuasively for a particular viewpoint
To summarise information from a source text
questions.explain: Descriptive writing aims to build a vivid, detailed picture rather than tell a story.

questions.q: Which sentence best uses figurative language to describe a storm?
options: The wind howled like a wounded animal clawing at the shutters
There was a storm and it was very windy outside
The weather report predicted rain later that day
It was raining and the temperature dropped
questions.explain: The simile 'like a wounded animal' is figurative language that creates a vivid, atmospheric image.

questions.q: You are describing a busy morning market. Which opening best establishes atmosphere?
options: Steam rose from stacked baskets as vendors' cries tangled with the clatter of coins
I went to the market and bought some fruit and vegetables
Markets are places where people buy and sell things
First I woke up, then I got dressed and left the house
questions.explain: The sensory detail of sight and sound establishes a vivid atmosphere suited to descriptive writing.

questions.q: In Section B, how many compositions must a candidate write?
options: One, chosen from a selection of descriptive and narrative titles
Two, one descriptive and one narrative
All four titles offered
Three, chosen freely
questions.explain: Candidates write a single composition, choosing one title from the descriptive and narrative options.

questions.q: What is the primary feature of narrative writing?
options: It tells a story with plot and characters
It lists factual instructions in order
It presents a balanced argument
It describes a static scene with no events
questions.explain: Narrative writing tells a story, developing plot and characters over time.

questions.q: Which sequence best describes an effective narrative structure?
options: Opening, development, climax, resolution
Conclusion, climax, opening, development
Climax, resolution, opening, development
Resolution, opening, climax, development
questions.explain: A well-shaped narrative moves from an opening through development to a climax and resolution.

questions.q: How can a writer build tension in a narrative?
options: By using short sentences and withholding information to create suspense
By resolving every problem in the first paragraph
By listing many characters' names at once
By copying dialogue directly from a source text
questions.explain: Short sentences and delayed information heighten suspense, a key narrative technique.

questions.q: You want the reader to share a single character's fears and uncertainty throughout a story. Which choice is most effective?
options: A consistent first-person narrator
An omniscient narrator who reveals everyone's thoughts
Frequent shifts between several narrators
No narrator, only stage directions
questions.explain: A consistent first-person viewpoint keeps the reader close to one character's feelings and uncertainty.

questions.q: What most clearly distinguishes descriptive from narrative writing?
options: Descriptive writing focuses on creating an image, while narrative writing focuses on telling a story
Descriptive writing must always be longer than narrative writing
Narrative writing cannot include any description
Descriptive writing is always written in the first person
questions.explain: Description centres on building a vivid impression, whereas narrative centres on events and plot.

questions.q: How long is Paper 2 (Directed Writing and Composition)?
options: 1 hour
1 hour 30 minutes
2 hours
3 hours
questions.explain: Paper 2 lasts 2 hours and covers both Directed Writing and Composition.

questions.q: Which of these is a key descriptive technique?
options: Appealing to the five senses to build a vivid picture
Providing a numbered list of events
Stating a thesis and a counter-argument
Summarising a plot in one sentence
questions.explain: Sensory detail that appeals to sight, sound, smell, touch and taste is central to effective description.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE First Language English (0500) syllabus; Paper 2: Directed Writing and Composition
